summary: The note describes the 'gradual release of responsibility' model in education, a teaching dynamic first named by Pearson and Gallagher in 1983. Based on Lev Vygotsky's ideas, instruction moves from explicit modeling to guided practice and then to activities that progressively make students independent learners. The goal is a point of 'planned obsolescence' of the teacher's role, where students take full responsibility for a task, including self-monitoring whether they apply a strategy appropriately.
one_line: Gradual release of responsibility is an instructional model, coined by Pearson and Gallagher in 1983, that shifts learning from teacher modeling to independent student work.
key_facts: Pearson & Gallagher (1983) coined the phrase 'gradual release of responsibility' to describe this dynamic in the classroom.
Similar models were identified and represented throughout the study and development of teaching and learning as a construct before the phrase was coined.
Pearson and Gallagher based their model on the ideas of the Russian educational theorist Lev Vygotsky.
The model envisioned instruction moving from explicit modeling and instruction to guided practice.
After guided practice, the model moves to activities that incrementally position students into becoming independent learners.
The note describes the teacher guiding students to a point of 'planned obsolescence' on the part of the teacher.
At the point of planned obsolescence, the student accepts total responsibility for the task.
Total responsibility includes determining whether or not the student is applying the strategy appropriately, referred to as self monitoring.
